sources.entry: How to Build a Web Framework in Less Than 20 Lines of Code

summary.title: Build a Web Framework In Less Than 20 Lines Of Code
summary.one_liner: You learn how to combine flexbox CSS utility classes and native DOM APIs (querySelector, forEach, addEventListener) into a tiny, jQuery-like starter kit for app-style web layouts.
keywords: native web apis instead of jquery
takeaways: Flexbox utility classes (.hbox, .vbox, .grow) cover most layout needs such as toolbars and vertical centering.
A .fill class with absolute positioning plus .scroll makes a desktop-app-style layout where only the list scrolls.
Flexbox order and flex rules can align form labels on the left and inputs in a second column.
A $ and $$ wrapper around document.querySelector and querySelectorAll replaces much of jQuery's selection role.
The article is explicitly a minimalist exploration, lacking routing, state management and a virtual DOM, so it is not a production framework.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a small set of CSS and JavaScript utilities presented as a 'web framework in under 20 lines.' It sets default fonts via npm packages (Source Pro fonts, Font Awesome), then defines flexbox classes for horizontal and vertical boxes, a grow class, scrolling and fill classes for fixed app-style panels, and flexbox-based form layout rules. On the JavaScript side it wraps document.querySelector and querySelectorAll as $ and $$ and uses forEach with addEventListener in place of jQuery-style helpers. The author includes a disclaimer that this is a lightweight starter kit rather than a full framework.
